insights.headline: Silver slides below $60 in a near-50% drawdown from January's peak; gold holds its two-month-low rebound.
insights.summary: Silver slipped below $60 an ounce on Thursday to about $59.35 — nearly 50% below January's record above $120 — even as analysts cited intact green-energy fundamentals and a widening supply deficit. Gold held its recovery from a two-month low, back above $4,100 as the dollar's rally stalled, though near-80% odds of a December Fed hike kept gains in check. In India, the rupee firmed 10 paise to 96.65 on likely RBI intervention, while MCX gold hovered near Rs 1.5 lakh per 10 grams with analysts seeing a negative near-term bias.
points: Spot silver fell to about $59.35, nearly 50% below January's record above $120; Metals Focus projects the deficit to widen to 46.3 million ounces this year.
Spot gold held above $4,100 after rebounding from a two-month low near $4,066; December-hike odds near 80% capped the bounce.
The rupee rose 10 paise to 96.65 in early trade on likely RBI intervention near the open.
Nuvama's Abhilash Koikkara sees a negative near-term bias on MCX gold (support Rs 1,45,000) and silver (support Rs 2,15,000).
The RBI raised the repo rate 25 bps to 5.50% — its first hike in nearly four years — shifting the stance to 'calibrated tightening'.

trending.title: Silver's 50% drawdown tests the bulls
trending.summary: Silver slid below $60, almost half of January's $120-plus peak, as high yields and a firm dollar kept pressure on. Yet analysts cite green-energy demand and a 46.3-million-ounce deficit.

trending.title: Gold's rebound hangs on the dollar's pause
trending.summary: Hawkish Fed minutes drove gold to a two-month low near $4,066; a stalling dollar let it reclaim $4,100. With December-hike odds near 80%, the bounce looks fragile.

trending.title: The rupee is doing half the work for Indian buyers
trending.summary: A 10-paise rise to 96.65 on likely RBI intervention cushioned the global selloff: MCX gold hovered near Rs 1.5 lakh per 10 grams, though analysts see a negative near-term bias.

trending.title: RBI's hawkish turn
trending.summary: The RBI's 25 bps hike to 5.50%, its first in nearly four years, plus signals of more tightening ahead, adds a domestic rate headwind for bullion.

trending.title: Central banks keep buying the dip
trending.summary: China added 740,000 oz in September, its biggest monthly rise in three years; the Dutch central bank moved 86 tonnes home; and gold ETFs drew a record $31B in Q3 despite the 8.5% slide.

items.title: Silver Slides Below $60: Why Analysts Still See A Shine Despite 50% Wipeout From Early 2026 Highs
items.summary: Spot silver slipped below $60 an ounce to about $59.35, nearly 50% below January's record above $120; MCX silver futures sit near Rs 2.21 lakh/kg versus early-2026 highs around Rs 4.2 lakh. Max Baecker of American Hartford Gold says volatility does not erase silver's green-energy fundamentals; Metals Focus's Philip Newman notes the global deficit is set to widen to 46.3 million ounces this year.

items.title: Gold prices recover from two-month low as dollar rally stalls
items.summary: Spot gold rose about 0.7% to $4,141 an ounce on Thursday as the dollar eased from an 18-month peak, recovering from the two-month low hit a day earlier when Fed minutes revived year-end rate-hike bets. US gold futures for December gained 0.6% to $4,165.10.

items.title: Gold, silver slump as Fed minutes keep December hike risk alive - Kitco PM Report
items.summary: Spot gold slid to about $4,110 an ounce and silver to roughly $59.67 in late US trading on Wednesday after minutes from the Fed's September meeting kept another year-end rate increase on the table. A firmer dollar and elevated long-end Treasury yields pressured non-yielding metals; traders now see an 80% chance of a December hike.

items.title: Gold near Rs 1.5 lakh/10 grams; silver rises as dollar eases from multi-month high
items.summary: MCX December gold rose Rs 557 to Rs 1,49,660 per 10 grams and December silver gained Rs 327 to Rs 2,23,888 per kg as the dollar eased from an 18-month peak. Spot gold added 0.5% to $4,133 after its lowest since August 5. Fed minutes showed a divided committee; traders price an 80% December hike. LKP Securities sees gold between Rs 1,48,000 and Rs 1,50,000 while dollar strength caps rallies.

items.title: RBI raises repo rate 25 bps to 5.5% in first hike in nearly four years, shifts stance to 'calibrated tightening'
items.summary: The RBI's six-member MPC voted unanimously to lift the repo rate from 5.25% to 5.50% on October 7 — its first hike since February 2023 — and moved the stance from neutral to 'calibrated tightening'. Governor Sanjay Malhotra said the inflation outlook is no longer benign, with CPI at 4.82% in August and FY27 inflation seen at 5.2%. The SDF rate moved to 5.25% and the MSF/bank rate to 5.75%.

items.title: RBI likely intervened near open to support rupee, traders say
items.summary: The rupee strengthened in early trade on Thursday, with traders saying the Reserve Bank likely intervened near the open to support it. The currency rose 10 paise to 96.65 against the US dollar.

items.title: Gold, silver price prediction: Will MCX Gold trade with negative bias? check outlook on October 8, 2026
items.summary: Nuvama's Abhilash Koikkara expects both metals to trade with a negative near-term bias. MCX gold (CMP Rs 149,375) faces resistance at Rs 1,52,000 with a downside target of Rs 1,45,000; MCX silver (CMP Rs 224,765) faces resistance at Rs 2,30,400 with a downside target of Rs 2,15,000 — a sell-on-rallies stance, per the analyst.

items.title: MCX gold stays below Rs 1.5 lakh as global prices fall 2 percent; what it means for investors
items.summary: MCX gold futures held below Rs 1.5 lakh per 10 grams on Wednesday as global bullion prices fell about 2% on a stronger dollar and higher US bond yields. The report breaks down what the slide means for Indian investors, from festive-season buying to the rupee's cushioning effect.

items.title: Gold extends slide to Rs 1.48 lakh per 10 gm in Delhi amid weak demand
items.summary: Gold prices in Delhi extended their slide to Rs 1.48 lakh per 10 grams as weak demand kept buyers away, tracking the global selloff that pushed bullion to two-month lows. The decline comes just ahead of the Diwali buying season, with elevated prices and the RBI's rate hike weighing on buyer sentiment.

items.title: Deutsche Bank sees silver supply deficit flipping to surplus by 2027
items.summary: Deutsche Bank says silver's multi-year supply deficit could flip to a surplus as early as 2027, as solar manufacturers cut silver use — photovoltaic silver demand may fall over 20% in 2026, with China's down about a third. Analyst Daniel Ghali expects spot silver to average about $70 an ounce in the second quarter of 2027.

items.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD cracks $60 as bears eye $56
items.summary: Silver fell below $60 an ounce to trade near $59.69 after the Fed minutes revived year-end rate-hike bets, and now sits below its 50-, 100- and 200-day moving averages. Mitrade's technical read sees a break below $59 exposing the August low of $56.57, with $62.09 as the first resistance.

items.title: MCX silver settles 0.51% higher at Rs 2,27,242 as weak US jobs data dims October Fed hike hopes
items.summary: Silver settled higher on MCX, buoyed by softer US jobs data that cut October Fed hike expectations — markets now see about a 78% chance the Fed holds this month — though a stronger dollar and rising Treasury yields capped gains. The 2026 global silver deficit is expected to widen to 46.3 million ounces, a sixth straight annual shortfall.

items.title: RBI signals more rate hikes ahead: Could 7.25% yield level become a near-term market reference point?
items.summary: After the RBI's 25 bps hike to 5.50% and the shift to 'calibrated tightening', economists see at least 50 bps of further hikes with the terminal rate near 6% by March 2027; the governor ruled out near-term cuts, saying only hikes or a pause lie ahead. The 10-year G-sec yield hardened to about 7.25%, which traders now watch as the near-term reference level.

items.title: Strait of Hormuz traffic falls to lowest in over two months after attacks, data shows
items.summary: Seven commodity vessels crossed the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday — the fewest since July 23 — after attacks on tankers hit a weekly high since the US-Iran war began, Kpler data showed. Crude crossings fell 27% from wartime highs to 10.1M bpd, though Gulf of Oman and Red Sea exports rose to 6.7M bpd, keeping total Middle East crude exports at pre-war levels.

items.title: China posts biggest monthly gold reserve increase in 3 years
items.summary: The People's Bank of China added 740,000 ounces of gold in September, lifting reserves to 77.47 million ounces — the largest monthly increase since September 2023 and the 23rd consecutive month of buying. China's foreign-exchange reserves dipped $38.1 billion to $3.4 trillion over the same month.

items.title: Dutch central bank transfers 86 tonnes of gold closer to home
items.summary: De Nederlandsche Bank moved about 86 tonnes of its gold from New York and Ottawa to London between March and August 2026, lifting London's share of its 612.4-tonne reserve from 18.1% to 32.1%. The bank said the move improves tradability and crisis readiness, citing rising geopolitical unrest.

items.title: Gold ETF rush defies 8.5% gold price slide
items.summary: Global gold ETFs drew a record $31 billion in the third quarter, including $10 billion in September, lifting holdings to a record 4,256 tonnes — even as bullion fell 8.5% in September to $4,176 an ounce, the World Gold Council said. BMO notes the split reflects futures selling rather than investors abandoning gold.

items.title: Gold price dips, but buyers remain cautious ahead of Diwali
items.summary: Gold has fallen roughly Rs 8,000 per 10 grams over the past month to about Rs 1.47 lakh (excluding GST), yet buyers in Pune remain cautious ahead of Diwali. Shoppers are choosing lighter jewellery and smaller token purchases, while jewellers report steady festive-season footfall.
